stem: Sound is produced by __________ objects.
solution: Sound is produced by vibrating objects.

stem: Sound travels in the form of __________ through a medium.
solution: Sound travels as waves, transferring energy through the medium without the medium moving as a whole.

stem: Sound waves are __________ waves, in which particles vibrate along the direction of wave travel.
solution: Sound waves are longitudinal — the medium's particles vibrate parallel to the direction of propagation.

stem: A sound wave consists of regions of __________ and rarefaction.
solution: A longitudinal sound wave has compressions (particles close together) and rarefactions (particles far apart).

stem: Sound needs a __________ to travel and cannot travel through a vacuum.
solution: Sound requires a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) and cannot travel through a vacuum.

stem: Sound travels fastest in __________.
solution: Sound travels fastest in solids (particles closest together) and slowest in gases.

stem: The number of vibrations (or waves) per second is called the __________.
solution: Frequency is the number of complete waves passing a point per second.

stem: The SI unit of frequency is the __________.
solution: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz); 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second.

stem: The distance between two consecutive compressions (or rarefactions) is the __________.
solution: The wavelength is the distance between two successive compressions or rarefactions.

stem: The maximum displacement of particles from their mean position in a wave is the __________.
solution: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from their rest (mean) position.

stem: The loudness of a sound depends on its __________.
solution: The greater the amplitude, the louder the sound.

stem: The pitch (shrillness) of a sound depends on its __________.
solution: The higher the frequency, the higher the pitch of the sound.

stem: The speed of a wave is related to frequency and wavelength by __________.
solution: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength (v = fλ).

stem: A sound wave of frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.66 m has a speed of __________.
The time taken to complete one vibration (one wave) is the __________.
solution: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation; it is the reciprocal of frequency.

stem: The range of frequencies audible to normal humans is about __________.
solution: Humans hear sounds of frequency roughly 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

stem: Sound of frequency above 20,000 Hz, which humans cannot hear, is called __________.
solution: Ultrasound has a frequency above 20 kHz, inaudible to humans.

stem: Sound of frequency below 20 Hz is called __________.
solution: Infrasound is below 20 Hz, inaudible to humans.

stem: The bouncing back of sound from a surface is called __________.
solution: Reflection of sound produces echoes; the laws of reflection apply to sound too.

stem: The repetition of a sound due to reflection from a distant surface is called an __________.
solution: An echo is a distinct repetition of a sound caused by its reflection.

stem: To hear a distinct echo, the reflecting surface must be at least about __________ away.
solution: The reflecting surface must be at least ~17 m away so that the reflected sound returns after ~0.1 s, enough to be heard separately.

stem: The technique that uses ultrasound to detect underwater objects and measure sea depth is __________.
solution: SONAR (Sound Navigation And Ranging) uses ultrasound echoes to detect objects and measure sea depth.

stem: SONAR works on the principle of __________ of sound.
solution: SONAR measures the time for an ultrasound pulse to reflect (echo) back from an object.

stem: Ultrasound is used in medicine to __________.
options: image internal organs and the developing foetus
solution: Ultrasound scans (sonography) image internal organs and are used to check a developing foetus.

stem: Ultrasound is also used to __________ (break) kidney stones.
solution: High-energy ultrasound can break kidney stones into fragments that leave the body naturally.

stem: Bats navigate and catch prey in the dark using __________.
solution: Bats emit ultrasound and detect the echoes (echolocation) to navigate and hunt in the dark.

stem: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is about __________.
solution: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air; it is much faster in water (~1500 m/s) and solids.

stem: The human ear detects sound because sound waves make the __________ vibrate.
solution: Sound waves cause the eardrum to vibrate, and these vibrations are passed on to the inner ear.

stem: The loudness of sound is measured in units called __________.
solution: Loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

stem: Unwanted, unpleasant sound that can be harmful is called __________.
solution: Noise is unpleasant, unwanted sound and can cause noise pollution.

stem: Thunder is heard some seconds after lightning is seen because __________.
options: sound travels much slower than light
solution: Light travels far faster than sound, so lightning is seen before the thunder is heard.

stem: The persistence of sound in a hall due to repeated reflections is called __________.
solution: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections in an enclosed space.

stem: Auditoriums have sound-absorbing materials on walls and ceilings to __________.
solution: Sound-absorbing materials reduce unwanted reverberation and echoes, improving sound quality.

stem: As the amplitude of a sound wave increases, the sound becomes __________.
solution: A larger amplitude gives a louder sound.

stem: As the frequency of a sound increases, its pitch becomes __________.
solution: Higher frequency corresponds to a higher (shriller) pitch.

stem: Ultrasound is preferred in cleaning and detecting flaws in metals because it __________.
options: has a high frequency and can penetrate and detect fine details
solution: High-frequency ultrasound penetrates materials and detects fine cracks/flaws and cleans intricate parts.

stem: In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium move __________ to the direction of wave travel.
solution: In a longitudinal wave, particles vibrate parallel (back and forth along) the direction of wave propagation.

stem: Compared to air, sound travels __________ in water.
solution: Sound travels faster in water than in air because water's particles are closer and denser.

stem: The reflection of ultrasound is used to measure the depth of the sea by measuring the __________.
options: time for the echo to return
solution: SONAR measures the time for an ultrasound echo to return, which gives the sea depth.

stem: A stethoscope works by __________ sound from the heart/lungs to the doctor's ears.
solution: A stethoscope guides (by multiple reflections) the sound of internal organs to the doctor's ears.

stem: Which of the following is an application of the reflection of sound?
solution: Megaphones and SONAR use the reflection of sound waves.

stem: Two sounds of the same loudness but different pitch differ in their __________.
solution: Pitch depends on frequency, so equally loud sounds of different pitch have different frequencies.

stem: In an ultrasound scan of a foetus, the ultrasound waves are __________ by the body's tissues.
options: reflected back to form an image
solution: Ultrasound waves reflect off tissues and the echoes are used to build an image (sonography).

stem: The energy of a sound wave is carried by the __________ of the medium.
options: movement of particles from source to ear
solution: Sound energy travels as vibrations pass from particle to particle; the particles themselves do not travel with the wave.

stem: Prolonged exposure to loud sound (high decibels) can cause __________.
solution: Loud noise over long periods can damage hearing and cause stress and other health problems.

stem: The frequency of a wave and its time period are related by __________.
solution: Frequency is the reciprocal of the time period (f = 1/T).

stem: An echo is heard clearly in a large empty hall but not in a small room because __________.
options: the reflecting surface must be far enough for the echo to be distinct
sound is louder in small rooms
solution: A distinct echo needs the reflecting surface far enough (≥~17 m); small rooms are too small.

stem: Sound waves are __________ waves.
solution: Sound travels as longitudinal waves, with particles vibrating along the direction of travel.

stem: The reflection of sound is used in the technique called __________.
solution: SONAR uses the reflection (echo) of ultrasound to detect underwater objects and measure depth.

stem: The loudness of sound is measured in __________.
solution: Loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Sound Waves: Characteristics and Applications' is that:
options: sound is a longitudinal wave needing a medium, characterised by frequency, wavelength, amplitude and speed, with applications like echoes, SONAR and ultrasound
solution: The chapter explains sound as a longitudinal wave, its characteristics (frequency, wavelength, amplitude, speed), reflection (echo, reverberation), and applications like SONAR and ultrasound.
